content.title: About
content.content: Limburger is a soft cheese known for its strong aroma, originating from the Limburg region of Germany. It has a creamy texture, pale yellow color, and a mild tang that intensifies with age.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese takes its name from the town of Limburg, where it was first produced in the 18th century.
Traditional Limburger is aged from 2 to 12 months; the longer the aging, the more pronounced the smell.
Its odor is often compared to foot sweat, onions or soap, making it a favorite among fans of pungent cheeses.
In the United States, Limburger is marketed as one of the “smelliest cheeses” and is often served in small tasting portions.
It is made from cow’s milk, sometimes enriched with a small amount of cream for a smoother mouthfeel.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Limburger provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Its calcium content contributes to bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic bacteria
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial microbes that can support gut microbiota.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids, which are heart‑friendly when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Limburger contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: The cheese is typically salty; excessive intake can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey should avoid this cheese.

items.title: Strong odor
items.content: The pungent smell may be off‑putting in public settings; it’s best enjoyed in private or well‑ventilated areas.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Limburger is usually served in thin slices on bread, crackers, or as part of a cheese board. It can be added to salads, baked dishes, or used in sauces where a bold flavor is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Limburger in its original packaging or tightly wrapped in plastic film in the refrigerator at +2‑+6 °C. For longer storage (over 2 weeks), wrap it in wax paper to preserve its aroma.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy, coconut filled are small sweets coated with milk or dark chocolate and filled with a fragrant coconut cream filling. They are popular as a treat for both children and adults, often served as a dessert or party snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The coconut filling is usually made from shredded coconut, sugar and butter, sometimes flavored with vanilla or rum.
Coconut‑filled chocolate candies are often associated with tropical flavors and are common in Caribbean and Southeast Asian cuisines.
These candies first appeared in the early 20th century as a variation of coconut bars covered in chocolate.
Toasting the shredded coconut before mixing enhances the coconut aroma.
Some recipes use white chocolate to highlight the light color of the coconut filling.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Coconut contains medium‑chain triglycerides that can be quickly used by the body for energy.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Shredded coconut provides dietary fiber that supports normal digestion.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Coconut supplies potassium, magnesium and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, creating a feeling of pleasure.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: These candies contain a notable amount of sugar, so they should be consumed in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Both chocolate and coconut make the product energy‑dense; large portions can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Coconut fat is primarily saturated fatty acids, which should be limited in individuals with heart disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies as a standalone snack, stir them into ice cream or yogurt, or use them as a sweet filling in baked goods. They are conveniently packaged for on‑the‑go consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent the chocolate from melting.

content.title: About
content.content: Glug is an energy drink made from natural extracts of goji berries, guarana, and vitamin B12. It is designed to boost alertness and concentration without a sharp sugar spike.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Glug contains goji berry extract, traditionally used in Tibetan medicine.
Guarana provides a sustained energy boost thanks to its natural caffeine.
Vitamin B12 helps support normal nervous system function.
The product contains no artificial colors or flavors.
Glug is sold in convenient 250 ml aluminum cans.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of guarana and vitamin B12 helps increase energy levels and reduce fatigue.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: Antioxidants from goji berries may enhance cognitive function and concentration.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Goji berries are rich in polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin B12 and other micronutrients contribute to normal immune system function.

items.title: Sugar‑free
items.content: Glug is sweetened with natural sugar substitutes, making it suitable for those monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Guarana contains caffeine; individuals sensitive to it should limit consumption.

items.title: Berry allergy
items.content: Some people may experience an allergic reaction to goji berries.

items.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
items.content: Pregnant or nursing women should consult a healthcare professional before use.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain drugs, such as CNS stimulants.

items.title: Excessive intake
items.content: Frequent consumption of energy drinks may lead to increased heart rate and anxiety.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Glug is best enjoyed cold, straight from the can. The recommended serving is one 250 ml can per day. Do not mix with alcohol or other caffeine sources.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Glug cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 24 hours.

green-peas-frozen-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Green peas, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Green peas are young pea pods harvested before full maturity. In the frozen form they are blanched quickly and flash‑frozen, preserving colour, taste and nutrients. The product is ready to eat without any added fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
Freezing retains more than 90 % of vitamin C compared with fresh peas.
Peas were domesticated over 7,000 years ago in the Mediterranean region.
In the United States, frozen green peas are among the top‑selling frozen vegetables.
Peas fix nitrogen in the soil, improving its fertility.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of cooked peas provides about 9 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps you feel full longer.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain folate, thiamine and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Peas contain purines, so people with gout should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add peas to soups, stews, salads, pasta dishes, or serve them as a side. They can be quickly reheated in the microwave or sautéed without oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen peas in a freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese ravioli are small pasta parcels filled with a creamy cheese mixture. Served without sauce, they let the delicate cheese flavor and tender pasta texture shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originated in Italy and have been made for over a thousand years.
Typical cheese fillings include ricotta, parmesan, or mozzarella, often seasoned with herbs.
When served without sauce, they are commonly drizzled with olive oil, fresh herbs, or a pat of butter.
The no‑sauce version is popular among those watching sugar and salt intake.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides a good source of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy cheeses contain calcium, which supports bone and dental health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 found in dairy is important for nervous system function and blood formation.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Skipping sauce reduces added sugars, beneficial for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: May provide probiotics (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Certain cheeses contain probiotic cultures that can aid gut health.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with milk protein allergy or lactose intolerance may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cheese fillings make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some cheeses are salty, which can be a concern for individuals with hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in the pasta
items.content: Traditional wheat pasta contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil the ravioli for 3–4 minutes until al dente, then drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle fresh herbs and grated parmesan. They can also be lightly pan‑fried for a crisp exterior.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried ravioli in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Fresh (frozen) ravioli should be kept at –18 °C and used within 2–3 months.
